h1: Large format porcelain tiling in Virginia Water

hero.intro: Virginia Water is known for its large detached properties, many close to the Wentworth Estate and its golf courses, set on generous plots with long driveways and, in a number of cases, gated or private road access. Properties range from substantial period houses to more recent executive-style builds, and the plot size generally gives us more flexibility on layout than a terraced property allows — including repositioning a shower to improve natural light, which changes how we think about tile colour and slab orientation as much as plumbing. We work fit-only, from £3,500, with you sourcing the sanitaryware, brassware, tiles and furniture.

sections.heading: Repositioning for light changes more than the plumbing
sections.body: When a layout allows us to move a shower or bath to catch more natural light — something the generous plots around Virginia Water often make possible — it's worth thinking about how that affects the tiling too. A large format slab with minimal grout breaks up far less light than a small-format tile grid does, so a brighter spot in the room reads even brighter once it's tiled in large porcelain. We'll talk through slab orientation and finish with you at survey stage, because a floor laid in one continuous direction toward a window reads differently to one broken into a grid.

sections.heading: Moving a waste run without hitting a structural wall
sections.body: The same plot size that gives scope for repositioning a shower also tends to give us room to relocate a waste run to accommodate a freestanding bath, without running into a structural wall the way a tighter, older terraced property often would. Whenever a layout changes, the new floor area gets exactly the same flatness check and full adhesive bed as the rest of the room — a layout change is not a shortcut around proper substrate prep.

sections.heading: What a flat substrate actually requires
sections.body: Large format porcelain slabs are rigid and unforgiving of dips in the floor beneath them — any variance shows as a rocking corner, a shadow line, or a stress crack once the slab takes weight. Before tiling, we check the substrate with a straight edge across the whole floor area, correct any low or high points with self-levelling compound or additional board, and only then start laying, with full adhesive coverage and levelling clips to keep every slab edge flush with its neighbour.

sections.heading: Arrange a survey
sections.body: We start with a paid £125 survey to check the substrate, talk through layout options including repositioning for light, and confirm access before you order tiles. Call or WhatsApp 07399 651836 to book a Virginia Water survey.

faqs.q: Can you reposition my shower to get more natural light?
faqs.a: Often, yes — the generous plots common around Virginia Water tend to give us more flexibility on layout than a smaller property, though it depends on the waste run and what the survey finds.

faqs.q: Does slab orientation matter for large format tiling?
faqs.a: Yes — laying slabs in a continuous direction toward a light source generally reads brighter and more seamless than breaking the floor into a grid, so we discuss orientation with you before fitting starts.

faqs.q: What happens if my subfloor isn't flat?
faqs.a: We correct it before tiling with self-levelling compound, additional boarding, or both — large format porcelain is rigid and will show or crack over an uneven substrate.

faqs.q: Do you handle gated or private road access?
faqs.a: Yes, we confirm access arrangements at survey stage so deliveries and our visits run smoothly on the day.

faqs.q: What's included in the fit-only service?
faqs.a: Strip-out, first-fix, tiling, plumbing and snagging — you buy the sanitaryware, brassware, tiles and furniture separately, with installs from £3,500.
